subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Rule re-read in context and cross-read at its target clause: §14.7.5's size-error case list (spec lines 21770-21784) -- case 6 is 'if standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, when an arithmetic operation on the intermediate data item would cause the new value to be outside of the range allowed for a standard-binary intermediate data item'; case 5 is the native leg and case 7 the standard-decimal leg. Expected behavior: an SBIDI overflow raises the size error condition + EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW, an underflow EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW, bounded by the §8.8.1.4.2 NOTE 3 range. READ: the exception names EXIST (ExceptionCatalog.cs:186/190 register EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION and EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW as level-3 Fatal), and the SIBLING legs are implemented -- CobolDec (CobolDec.cs:59, :125, :423, :431) raises EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW/-UNDERFLOW citing §8.8.1.5.2 r2, the decimal128 SDIDI range (§14.7.5 case 7), and CobolNum.cs:292 raises the native D1 escape-boundary overflow (§14.7.5 case 5). NO code implements case 6: grep of src/ for the SBIDI bound constants (2**16384 / 2**16271 / 2**-16494 / 2**-16382) returns nothing, and no range check anywhere is keyed on ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary. The gate is upstream anyway: DataBinder.BindDeclarations (DataBinder.cs:318-320) fails the compile with COBOL0806 before any statement is bound, so the mode's arithmetic never executes. BOTH halves unimplemented (overflow AND underflow), so this is not a PARTIAL. Editions 2014,2023 by the F.2 item 3 / E.2 item 21 derivation recorded on GR-8.8.1.4.2-1. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an SBIDI intermediate with its §8.8.1.4.2 NOTE 3 bounds checked at every arithmetic step, plus goldens driving one overflow (2**16384-scale product) and one underflow (below 2**-16494) under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY with and without ON SIZE ERROR. No qualifying test today. || UPHELD: I re-read §14.7.5's case list at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:21764-21784 myself -- case 6 is verbatim as quoted and is the ONLY standard-binary leg; case 1 ('if the rules for evaluation of exponentiation are violated') and the no-SIZE-ERROR-phrase rule 1 below it are the EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION route used by GR-8.8.1.4.4-4. I independently confirmed the two halves are absent and the sibling legs present: `grep -rn 'EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW|EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW' src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime` shows ExceptionCatalog.cs:188 L3('EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW', EcFatality.Fatal) and :190 L3('EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW', EcFatality.Fatal) (the adjudicator wrote :186/:190; :186 is EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION and :188 is EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW -- a one-line slip, not a substantive error), and `grep -rn '16384|16494|16382|16271' src/ --include=*.cs` returns EMPTY, so no SBIDI bound is checked anywhere. PARTIAL was considered and rejected on the same grounds the adjudicator gives: neither the overflow nor the underflow half exists, and ground rule 5's 'one of two halves verified => PARTIAL' needs at least one half implemented. The rule is unreachable behind the DataBinder.cs:318 gate regardless. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).
